data.name: NeverBound
data.detailed_description:
NeverBound is the gravity-shifting shooter that adds another dimension to the traditional FPS. Take part in mind-bending combat and puzzles in multi-gravity environments. You are as dangerous from below as you are from above. Scale the walls and ceilings, or use long hallways as vertical drops, as you outmaneuver your enemies.

NeverBound takes place in a future where a fifth fundamental force of nature has been discovered. The technology quickly revolutionizes society and allows humans to simulate arbitrary directions of gravity. A new architecture for a new age arises, STRUCT, in which the flows of populous are greatly improved due to its multi-gravity nature.

The rules have changed. High ground is relative.


  • Surprise your enemies from the inverted floor above.
  • Throw grenades that can fall in any direction. Loop them around corners or let them float in Zero-G.
  • Beat down your enemies and disrupt their gravity fields with the Gravity Baton.
  • Conjure insurmountable forces to crush your foe under intense gravity.

Join the discussion!

reviews.review:
A Revised Review 28 Aug 2018:
Imagine playing a First Person Shooter (FPS) where any surface of a cube, inside and outside, could be the ground upon which you stand.
Imagine one of those optical illusion drawings where all the staircases meet with each other at the oddest angles, and you could walk on anyof those staircases.
Imagine a game where your sense of up and down is all relative, a game with the topsy/turvy orientation like you were watching Doctor Strange or Inception.

Neverbound is a future-based FPS where nearly any surface can be used to move around and attack.  While that may sound fun, your enemies have the same ability, and you can never be quite sure where the next attack is coming on (well, you eventually can, but I feel dramatic right now).  From what I have played of the game (and that is everything), this is a single-player game.

The enemy soldier AI gets the job done, but they are more of a threat because you don't know where they are coming from.  Be careful though, they seem to respawn sporadically, so just because you cleared out a room doesn't mean it stays clear indefinitely.  They also have mounted and flying turrets you need to watch out for (hint: shoot the wings on the flying turrets).  Because the enemy soldiers can come from any direction, when you shoot them, they don't always fall 'down'; they can fall up and sideways as well.  It's pretty fun to shoot somebody from an adjacent surface, watch how they fall, and wonder 'what the heck!'.  Ypu also have the ability to 'force-grab' the weapon from your enemies hands, which comes in handy (easier to disarm than shoot down on occassion).

The variety of sci-fi weapons is decent (a basic rifle, a police-type baton (which has a pretty good kick), a laser type weapon that doesn't run out but can overheat, a sniper rifle, and a gravity-defying grenade (which I never really used outside of the training mission).

The level design is amazing, starting off with something along the lines of a training mission, and culminates with a truly magnificient level called 'Leap of Faith', where combat, Inception-style, comes alive.  There are also levels (e.g., Blitz) that are more arcade-like, where the goal is to get the high score; for myself, patience is key in Blitz.
Because nearly surface can be used to move, moving around the level itself has puzzle-like qualities (which is a pleasant change from shooting all the time), but be careful, sometimes the level, and not the enemy soldiers, can be the greater threat.

The controls are a mixture of teleporrt and free locomotion.  They are teleport pads that can directly tranport you to a different surface, and for that the teleport feature is needed.  Turning is uinfortunately limited to snap turning, and not smooth.
Movement and aiming fell pretty solid, with the occassional bout of 'I could've sworn I shot that guy'.
Every so often, I would get a glitch where the level would momentarily freeze, but usually recovered, and one the first main level, I had a couple of glitches to where I was in infinite free-fall..

This is not only a game that provides merely a different perspective, but shows you gameplay from nearly every perspective. When I got done with the 'Leap of Faith' level, I felt like a kid again, which is all I could ever ask from a game.

I found the game worth the price because of what I got out of it; your mileage may vary.  If you want to experience sci-fi combat from a lot of prespectives, I would easily recommend this.

Any issues I had with this game, I usually relayed to the developers through their Discord Channel.  They are very kind folk, and take the time to respond to what you have to say.

For an Early Access game, I'm glad I took the plunge.
